L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (183+ days in a calendar year) are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents only on Belarus-source income. Most personal income is taxed at a flat 13%, and business income of registered individual entrepreneurs at 16% (MyExpatTaxes; TaxAtlas). Simplified and professional-income regimes exist for some activities (not verified). Sanctions sharply limit foreign platforms and payments (see W1).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT is 20%, with reduced 10% and 0% bands. A business registers with the Ministry of Taxes and Duties once it makes taxable supplies (no turnover threshold reported). Foreign suppliers of electronic services to Belarusian consumers register separately under the foreign e-services regime (since 2018).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money; major freelance and payment platforms exclude residents (sanctions or payment-partner restrictions). No clean workaround: these platforms exclude residents, for sanctions or payment-partner reasons depending on the country. Using someone else's account, a foreign address or a VPN to appear elsewhere breaches their terms, risks frozen funds, and can breach sanctions law. Do not do it. Legal options are limited to what local banks and licensed local channels allow (see P1/P2), and they change with sanctions policy, so check the current status before relying on any route.
